conditions.text: All three events ran app version 3.1.0 on iOS 18.4 on an iPhone15,2 (device model iPhone15,2), so reproduce on that combination first.

In every event push was deliverable with OS permission ALLOWED and provider registration REGISTERED, and the profile was consistent; these held uniformly but the packet does not establish they are causally required.
What varies is the lead-in: one event has an empty prefix and one has a single unmapped sdk.session step, so that prefix is not a precondition.

Two commits touch the culprit file src/modules/jobs/apply.ts and are leads only, not confirmed causes: c31a111 "MEI-40: Apply to jobs from the detail page" and c31b222 "MEI-41: Cache job detail responses".
Coverage is incomplete: one event had no breadcrumbs and one had unmapped steps, so the five-step path rests on 2 of 3 events.

missing_evidence_questions.text: What did the event with no breadcrumbs actually do before the crash, and does it follow the same /jobs to apply path?
What is the UNMAPPED sdk.session step, and does mapping it change the reconstructed prefix?
Is the 500 from POST /api/applications the cause of the undefined value read at apply.ts:57, or does the crash also occur when that call succeeds?
Which object is undefined at apply.ts:57, and does the job detail caching introduced by c31b222 or the apply flow added in c31a111 leave it unset?
Does the crash reproduce outside app 3.1.0 on iOS 18.4 / iPhone15,2, or are those versions genuinely required?

steps_prose.text: Navigate to /jobs (seen in 2 of the 3 events, support 0.67).
Tap a job card (li.job-card) in the list.
Land on the job detail route /jobs/detail.
The backend call POST /api/applications returns 500, and the crash surfaces in submitApplication at src/modules/jobs/apply.ts line 57 reading 'jobId' off an undefined value.

One of the three events reached this sequence with no preceding steps, and another started with an unmapped sdk.session step, so nothing is required before the /jobs navigation as far as the packet shows.

summary.text: The incident is a TypeError, "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'jobId')", thrown in submitApplication at src/modules/jobs/apply.ts:57 when a user taps Apply on a job detail page and the POST /api/applications call returns 500; it was reconstructed from 3 events.
